jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Arkansas, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Arkansas, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Arkansas Senate, Arkansas House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Arkansas district map, what district am I in, Arkansas Senate district, Arkansas House district, Arkansas congressional district, Arkansas school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Arkansas, and who represents you there.

head.title: Arkansas district lookup — districtry Arkansas
head.description: Tap the map or search an Arkansas address: county, Arkansas Senate, Arkansas House and U.S. House districts — and who represents you.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Arkansas, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Arkansas — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search an Arkansas address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 4 congressional districts — the largest districts Arkansas carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 4 features for Arkansas, measured 2026-10-13. Arkansas did not redraw for 2026: the 120th-Congress map and the 119th's (layer 4) carry the same four districts with identical land areas, every one differing by 0.00000% of its area.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Court of Appeals District
layers.rank_note: 7 Court of Appeals districts of whole counties, 19,683 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — smaller on average than a congressional district (34,445 km2), larger than a judicial circuit (4,921 km2)

source.answers: The Court of Appeals district covering the point: the counties it is made of, and how many of the court's twelve judges its voters elect.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric (TIGERweb State_County layer 1) by ar/scripts/build_ar_court_districts.py, following Act 1812 of 2003's list of each district's counties as the Arkansas GIS Office's metadata for its Appeals Court Districts layer quotes it (read 2026-10-16), and held county by county to that layer. The act was not read at source: the official Code is published by LexisNexis behind a page that needs a browser's scripts, and the two free copies tried refuse this project's client.
Arkansas Judiciary — the Court of Appeals' district map page, which lists each district's judgeships (two in Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, one in Districts 5 and 7)

source.people: No judge is named yet: the court's own pages name every judge, and this app does not publish them yet; recorded as gap ar-appeals-judges. The card says how many of the court's twelve judges the district elects and links the court's district page, which names them.

layers.label: Judicial Circuit
layers.rank_note: 28 judicial circuits of whole counties, 4,921 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — smaller on average than a Court of Appeals district, larger than a State Senate district (3,937 km2)

source.answers: The judicial circuit covering the point: its circuit court, how many judges the circuit's voters elect, and whether a federal court order divides it into election subdistricts.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric (TIGERweb State_County layer 1) by ar/scripts/build_ar_court_districts.py, following the Administrative Office of the Courts' circuit judge directory, which lists each judge under every county the judge serves (read 2026-10-16), and held county by county to the Arkansas GIS Office's Circuit Court Districts layer. The five circuits a federal court order (Hunt v. State of Arkansas) divides into election subdistricts are drawn whole.
Arkansas GIS Office — the Circuit Court Districts layer's metadata, which summarises the court order

source.people: No judge is named yet: the directory names every circuit judge, and this app does not publish them yet; recorded as gap ar-circuit-judges. The card gives the circuit's number of judges, from the directory, and links it.

layers.label: Arkansas Senate District
layers.rank_note: 35 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Arkansas Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 35 features, measured 2026-10-13. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ar-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Arkansas State Legislature's own member list and each member's own page (name, party, e-mail and the member's page). A member the Legislature's page marks as resigned or deceased is not carried, so a seat with no current member reads as vacant: Senate 1 and 18 on 2026-10-13.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 75 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, its county judge, and the justices of the peace on its quorum court.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 75 features, measured 2026-10-13.

source.people: ar-county-officials.json, read on 2026-10-13: the county judge from the Arkansas Judiciary's directory of county judges and clerks (with the office telephone, and the office address only where the Association of Arkansas Counties prints the same one), and the county's justices of the peace from the Association of Arkansas Counties' page for the county, listed as the association lists them, without a district; the Quorum Court District layer names each district's justice where a source says who it is. Recorded as gap ar-quorum-court.

layers.label: Arkansas House District
layers.rank_note: 100 House districts — smaller on average than a county, larger than a school district

source.answers: The Arkansas House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 100 features, measured 2026-10-13.

source.people: ar-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Arkansas State Legislature's own pages on the same terms as the Senate roster; House 8 read vacant on 2026-10-13.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 234 unified (K-12) districts covering the whole state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 234 features for Arkansas, measured 2026-10-13.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Arkansas's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members has been established here; the state's school directory lists no board members. Recorded as gap ar-school-board-members.
source.applies: Arkansas — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary and secondary tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in Arkansas (0 features each, measured 2026-10-13), and the 234 unified districts' Census land area sums to exactly the 75-county total (134,659 km2).

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 942 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside Arkansas

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='05'. 942 features in Arkansas's box, measured 2026-10-13.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Arkansas. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (the Texas test point gives 75570).

layers.label: Quorum Court District
layers.rank_note: 775 justice of the peace districts in 75 counties, pre-built from the state's own layer; smaller on average than a ZIP Code area, larger than a city or town

source.answers: The justice of the peace district covering the point, its county, the county judge who presides over the quorum court, and the district's justice where a source says who it is.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — FEATURESERVICES/Boundaries, layer 19 (JUSTICE_PEACE_DISTRICT), credited to the Arkansas Secretary of State: every county's justice of the peace districts in one statewide layer, pre-built and shipped with the app; 775 districts in 75 counties, each county numbered 1 to N at one of the four counts Arkansas Code 14-14-402 allows, measured 2026-10-13. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ar-county-officials.json, read on 2026-10-13: each county judge from the Arkansas Judiciary's directory of county judges and clerks, and each county's justices of the peace from the Association of Arkansas Counties' page for that county. A district's justice is named from the county's own site where it numbers them (20 counties, measured 2026-10-13), and elsewhere from the association's 2024 general election results for justices of the peace, updated 17 December 2024, only while the association's current list for the county still includes that winner; a district whose winner has left, or cannot be matched, says so and names no one. Recorded as gap ar-quorum-court.

layers.label: Township
layers.rank_note: 820 townships in 75 counties, pre-built from the state's own layer — median 103.5 km2 (mean 168.0), measured 2026-10-15: just smaller than a justice of the peace district (median 108.2 km2), larger than a city or town

source.answers: The township containing the point, and its county.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — FEATURESERVICES/Boundaries, layer 57 (TOWNSHIP_POLITICAL_DIVISION), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app (ar/scripts/build_ar_townships.py); 820 townships in 75 counties, measured 2026-10-15. Chosen over the Census's map, which differs from it in at least 27 counties: TIGERweb still draws 38 townships in Washington County, where a 2013 county court order upheld in Clowers v. Edwards (2020) left 3.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER NAMED. A township has no government of its own, but its voters elect a constable for a two-year term (Arkansas Constitution, article 7, section 47). No source naming constables by township has been read, so the card says so and names nobody.

layers.label: Fire District
layers.rank_note: 971 fire districts, pre-built from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer — 140.9 km2 mean area (median 123.9), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a township (168.0), larger than a school board zone (113.9)

source.answers: Every fire district the point is in on the Arkansas GIS Office's map, with the counties each serves, the date the map gives its lines and, for 90 districts, the record the GIS Office holds for them. Where the map labels ground rather than naming a district ("Unserviced" and three others), the card quotes the label.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — FIRE_DISTRICTS, layer 59 of its Boundaries service: the map state law (A.C.A. § 12-10-329, as the layer's own description puts it) has every fire district keep, certified by the mayor, county judge or county fire coordinator, and send to the GIS Office. 971 districts from 973 records, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_fire_districts.py and shipped with the app. It credits the Arkansas GIS Office and states no licence.

source.people: NO NAMES. The GIS Office's map names each fire district and the counties it serves but not who runs it, and no statewide list of who runs Arkansas's fire districts has been read, so the card names no one rather than guessing; recorded as gap ar-fire-district-boards.
source.applies: Arkansas — statewide. The districts overlap in places and leave less than 1% of the state in no district, so the card lists every district the map puts the point in.

layers.label: School Board Zone
layers.rank_note: 965 zones on the boards of 176 school districts, pre-built from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer — 113.9 km2 mean area (median 58.4), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a township (168.0), larger than a voting precinct (47.19)

source.answers: The zone a school board elects a member from, and the school district whose board it is. Where a board has resolved to elect every member at large and is changing a seat at a time, the card says when it resolved.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — SCHOOL_BOARD_ZONES, layer 32 of its Boundaries service, which the Arkansas Secretary of State compiles “to aid in election administration and future redistricting”: 965 zones on 176 school districts, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_school_board_districts.py and shipped with the app. It credits the Secretary of State, is provided as is, and states no licence.

Arkansas GIS Office — its notes of 9 April 2026 on the school board zone update, naming the twelve boards that resolved to elect every member at large and when; read through the Internet Archive's copy of 13 May 2026, because the page itself now redirects

source.people: NO NAMES YET. No statewide list of Arkansas's school board members has been found — the Department of Education's report-card feed carries no board field — so the card names no one rather than guessing; recorded as gap ar-school-board-members.
source.applies: The 176 Arkansas school districts whose boards elect some or all members from zones. A board elected wholly at large has no zones, and the empty card says so.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 2,920 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer — 47.19 km2 mean area, land and water (median 7.42), measured 2026-10-15 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a township (168.0), larger than a city or town (13.11 km2 of land)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — ELECTION_PRECINCTS, layer 11 of the Boundaries service, published with the Secretary of State's Elections Division from what each county's voter registration system holds; 2,920 precincts in 2,928 records (a precinct in pieces is joined into one), pre-built for the state by ar/scripts/build_ar_precincts.py and shipped with the app. The GIS Office's web map calls the boundaries a public domain record.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 501 incorporated cities and towns, live from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 501 features for Arkansas (315 cities, 186 towns), measured 2026-10-13.

source.people: In the 19 cities above 25,000 people, the mayor and every council member or director, written down from each city's own pages and proved against those pages by ar/scripts/build_ar_city_councils.py, which fails when a name is no longer on the page it cites (ar/data/app/ar-city-councils.json, 174 seats read 2026-10-16). Each seat says whether its ward's own voters or the whole city elect it, measured from the ballot because nothing the state publishes records it. The Arkansas Municipal League's statewide directory is not used: it gives no ward or position and disagreed with five of the twelve cities' own pages where both could be compared. Arkansas's other 482 cities and towns name nobody yet, recorded as gap ar-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Arkansas — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: City Council District
layers.rank_note: 56 council wards and districts in the 12 cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by ward, pre-built from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer — 27.2 km2 mean area (median 23.7, from 4.2 in Texarkana to 74.3 in Fort Smith), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — ranked just after City or Town, which each one divides, so a ward draws on top of its city

source.answers: The city council ward or district containing the point, in the 12 Arkansas cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by ward, and the members its own voters elect.

boundary.label: Arkansas GIS Office — MUNICIPAL_WARDS, layer 50 of its Boundaries service: 852 wards of 262 cities and towns, measured 2026-10-16, of which the 56 wards of these twelve cities are pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_city_wards.py and shipped with the app. It carries the Arkansas GIS Office's copyright line, states no licence, and describes itself as not representing exact legal boundaries.

source.people: The members each ward's own voters elect, from the same city council roster the City or Town card reads (ar/data/app/ar-city-councils.json), written down from each city's own pages and proved against them by ar/scripts/build_ar_city_councils.py. Which seats a ward elects was measured from the ballot, and the builder's check holds every drawn ward to a seat its voters elect and every such seat to a drawn ward.
source.applies: The 12 Arkansas cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by ward: Benton, Conway, Fayetteville, Fort Smith, Hot Springs, Little Rock, North Little Rock, Paragould, Pine Bluff, Russellville, Sherwood and Texarkana. The state's map carries wards for 250 more cities and towns. Seven of them are the other cities above 25,000, which elect every seat by the whole city, so a ward there elects no one of its own; the rest are not drawn because this app does not name those councils.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-13: 522 points in Arkansas's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Arkansas — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

layers.label: Fire & EMS Station
layers.rank_note: nearest fire and EMS stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest fire and EMS stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 51 (Fire Stations/EMS Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-13: 1,619 points in Arkansas's envelope, within 381 of the service's 2,000-record cap, which is why the paging is not optional.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a fire and EMS station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Arkansas — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question, and the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you; the Fire District layer draws the state's map of fire districts. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

source.answers: The three nearest post offices to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

Measured 2026-10-13: 812 points in Arkansas's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a post office is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Arkansas — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. anchor_point.note: the State Capitol, Little Rock, Pulaski County

negative_point.note: near New Boston, Bowie County, TEXAS, south of the Red River that forms the state line there — outside Arkansas and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-13: TIGERweb's county layer names Bowie County, Texas at this point (control: the Capitol anchor returns Arkansas), and the Census's ZIP layer answers 75570 there, which is the neighbouring-state answer the ZIP layer's coverage test exists to hide. TEXAS BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT and none is planned next; Mississippi and Louisiana, both on the next-states list, were passed over so this point does not have to move when either goes live, and the point sits well west of the Texas–Louisiana line.

geometry.note: The whole-Arkansas outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 75-county fabric.
The 75 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 4 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120).
The 775 justice of the peace districts of all 75 counties, from the state's own layer (ar/scripts/build_ar_quorum_court_districts.py).
The 820 townships of all 75 counties, from the state's own layer (ar/scripts/build_ar_townships.py).

Every Arkansas voting precinct, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.97% with zero overlaps; an exact 2,920 count on the drawn file, after the eight records that are further pieces of seven precincts are joined into them). 9.3 MB, 2.44 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

Every Arkansas school board zone, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_school_board_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 400-point agreement gate on every board's extent, measured 99.99% with zero overlaps; an exact 965 count, after the Jasper district's zone 3, published in two pieces, is joined into one). 5.1 MB, 1.40 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

Every Arkansas fire district, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_fire_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 400-point agreement gate on each set of counties' extent, measured 99.98%, with no point in two drawn districts where the source has one or none; an exact 971 count, after Siloam Springs, filed in three records, is joined into one). 6.6 MB, 1.99 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The 56 wards of the 12 cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by ward, pre-built by ar/scripts/build_ar_city_wards.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Arkansas GIS Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 4,800-point agreement gate over the twelve cities' extents, measured 99.98% with zero overlaps). 300 KB, 82 KB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.
The 7 Court of Appeals districts, dissolved from the county fabric by ar/scripts/build_ar_court_districts.py following Act 1812 of 2003's county lists.
The 28 judicial circuits, dissolved from the county fabric by ar/scripts/build_ar_court_districts.py following the circuit judge directory's county lists.

rosters.note: U.S. House (AR) roster, refreshed weekly by update-ar-congress-roster.yml.

Arkansas Senate roster from the Arkansas State Legislature's own member list and pages, one record per seat, refreshed weekly. A vacant seat carries a record saying so, so the floor is the chamber's size; Senate 1 and 18 read vacant on 2026-10-13.
Arkansas House roster on the same terms; House 8 read vacant on 2026-10-13.

Every county's judge (the Arkansas Judiciary's directory) and justices of the peace (the Association of Arkansas Counties), one record per county, built by update-ar-county-officials.yml. That job is scheduled weekly but has not completed since 2026-10-13, because the association's site answers its requests from GitHub's servers with HTTP 403 (measured 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15), so the file stays as read on 2026-10-13 and every card states that date.

The mayor and council of each of the 19 cities above 25,000 people, keyed by Census place id, written down from each city's own pages and proved against them by ar/scripts/build_ar_city_councils.py, whose --check holds the file to its seats file, its record of every page read and the drawn wards. Every page it cites is re-read weekly (watch-city-council-pages.yml, listed in the North Carolina worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance), which opens a tracking issue when a name has gone from its page and never edits the file; the seats file is changed by hand (ar/WATCH.md).
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.
